name: configure_cia_timer_interrupt
description: Stores a handler routine address in a shared word, programs the CIA-B timer and control registers with fixed values, and enables interrupt bits through the interrupt enable register. It also clears a counter field in the working record before returning.

name: clear_flag_set_dma_interrupts
description: Clears one bit in a shared flag byte, then writes a fixed sequence of constants to the DMA control and interrupt enable registers. The facts show it also reads the joystick and disk status port, so it is part of the device setup sequence.

name: scale_channel_levels_and_step
description: Calls a setup helper, then multiplies four table bytes by a current level and shifts each product down into spaced words of the working record. It finally moves a level byte one unit toward its previous value.

name: store_scaled_step_difference
description: Multiplies a shared value by a constant and divides the product by the same value, then stores in the working record the byte difference between two successive scaled counter values.

name: run_countdown_sequencer_step
description: Returns zero when a shared enable byte is clear. Otherwise it decrements a countdown in the record, and while it runs it dispatches four channels through a jump table; when it expires it reloads the countdown, clears four table entries, advances a wrapping index and points the record at the next table entry, while also touching the CIA-B timer control register.

name: write_timer_and_request_registers
description: Writes a counter value, a derived value and a copied word to shared globals that the facts identify as the CIA-B interrupt and control registers, the DMA control register and the interrupt request register. The final write sets the top bit of the value, which those registers treat as the enable flag.

name: reset_audio_channel_registers
description: Adjusts a shared value, then writes eight table entries into the pointer and length registers of all four audio channels, followed by a final constant write to the interrupt request register.

name: call_two_helper_routines
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available and the description rests only on the listed facts. The routine is called by one unnamed routine, calls two others across its 59 instructions, and touches no hardware registers.

name: find_table_entry_under_limit
description: Selects a nibble of the input byte according to a phase counter stored in the record, then scans a table row of up to 36 words for the first entry that does not exceed a stored limit. It writes that matching word to an output field, or leaves the output unchanged when the zero flag is set.

name: decrease_position_with_floor
description: Subtracts a delta from a position field in the record and raises the position to a fixed minimum when it falls below that floor. The result is copied into an output field.

name: step_value_toward_target
description: Calls a helper, then moves a position field toward a target field by a step size taken from another field. When the remaining distance is smaller than the step, it snaps the position to the target and copies the result to an output field.

name: add_delta_reset_to_reference
description: Adds a delta to a position field and, when the delta exceeds a second input value, replaces the position with a reference field from the record. The position is then copied to an output field.

name: set_level_offset_when_flagged
description: When the flag byte is nonzero, stores the input nibble byte in the record. It then looks up a table value by an index from the record byte, scales it by the low nibble, negates it when the sign bit is set, and writes the position plus this offset to the output. It adds a shifted amount of the stored byte into a second record field.

name: offset_position_by_table_value
description: Looks up a table value by an index from the record byte, scales it by the low nibble of the stored byte, negates it when the sign bit is set, and writes the position plus this offset to the output. It adds a shifted amount of the stored byte into a second record field.

name: relay_adjust_level_by_nibble
description: Calls a helper, then adjusts a byte level in the record using the input byte. A zero high nibble subtracts the low nibble and clamps the level at zero, while a nonzero high nibble adds it and clamps at a fixed ceiling.

name: adjust_level_by_nibble
description: Adjusts a byte level in the record using the input byte. A zero high nibble subtracts the low nibble and clamps the level at zero, while a nonzero high nibble adds it and clamps at a fixed ceiling.

name: store_level_byte
description: Stores the input byte directly into a level field of the working record and returns.

name: set_index_scaled_clear_counter
description: Stores the input word multiplied by four into an index field of the record and resets a counter field to zero.

name: store_byte_and_call_helper
description: Stores its byte argument into a shared global and then calls a helper routine. The branch for large values assigns the same byte again, so it has no net effect.

name: advance_position_by_stored_step
description: Copies a nonzero input byte into a step field of the record when present. It then adds scaled multiples of that step byte to a 16-bit field and to a 32-bit field, moving both by the stored value.

name: stub_empty_return
description: The routine body is only a return, so it performs no work.

name: call_six_helper_routines
description: The decompiler timed out, so this description rests on the listed facts only. The routine runs in the reference trace, is called by one routine and makes six calls across 30 instructions, and writes to the first custom chip register.

name: write_jump_patch_words
description: Calls a routine through a pointer, then writes a sequence of constant words that encode a jump to a handler into memory and touches the copper list pointer register. The decompiled body ends in bad instruction data, so its tail is unreliable.

name: check_status_write_patch_words
description: Calls a routine through a pointer, writes jump-encoded words and a fixed constant pattern into memory, then compares a returned status code against a fixed value. On a match it calls a helper with a fixed argument and another routine. The body ends in bad instruction data and references the text 'highs'.

name: xor_decrypt_memory_block
description: Calls two helper routines, then XORs a block of memory bytes with a counter that counts down from a fixed start, and returns a fixed status value. The routine's entry is taken by address.

name: call_single_helper_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are available. The routine is taken by address and executed in the reference run, is called by one routine and makes one call across 15 instructions.

name: write_call_patch_copper_pointer
description: Writes constant words that encode a call to a routine, along with a fixed value, into memory, and touches the copper list pointer register. The decompiled body ends in bad instruction data, so nothing beyond those writes is shown.

name: emit_jump_word_for_handler
description: Writes a jump-encoded word followed by the address of a handler routine into memory. The decompiled body then ends in bad instruction data, so nothing further is shown.

name: dispatch_two_helper_calls
description: The decompiler timed out, so this description rests on the listed facts only. The routine is taken by address, is called by two routines, and makes two calls across 15 instructions.

name: relay_single_helper_call
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are available. The routine is taken by address, is called by one routine and makes one call across 15 instructions.

name: write_call_patch_words
description: Writes constant words that encode a call and a value fixed in the code into memory, then touches the copper list pointer register. The decompiled body ends in bad instruction data, so its tail is unreliable.

name: write_jump_patch_pair
description: Writes a jump-encoded word followed by the address of a routine into memory. The decompiled body then ends in bad instruction data, so nothing further is shown.

name: forward_single_helper_call
description: The decompiler timed out, so this description rests on the listed facts only. The routine is taken by address, is called by one routine and makes one call across 10 instructions.

name: call_handler_with_block_address
description: Calls a routine through a pointer, writes jump-encoded words and a fixed constant pattern into memory, then compares a returned status code against a fixed value. On a match it calls a routine through a pointer with a fixed memory location and another routine. The body ends in bad instruction data and references the text 'highs'.

name: xor_memory_block_with_counter
description: Calls a routine through a pointer, then XORs a block of memory bytes with a counter that counts down from a fixed start, and returns a fixed status value. It is called by four routines and references the text 'highs'.

name: xor_block_after_helper_call
description: Calls a helper routine, then XORs a block of memory bytes with a counter that counts down from a fixed start, and returns a fixed status value. It is called by one routine.

name: xor_block_and_return_status
description: Calls a helper routine, then XORs a block of memory bytes with a counter that counts down from a fixed start, and returns a fixed status value. The listed facts show the entry is taken by address.

name: xor_bytes_by_descending_counter
description: Takes its input value as a starting count, XORs that many memory bytes with a counter that counts down, and returns the input unchanged. It is called by six routines, calls a three-instruction register-copy helper, and references the text 'highs'.

name: return_helper_result_low_half
description: Calls a routine through a pointer and, when the high half of its 64-bit result is nonzero, returns the unchanged input register pair; otherwise it returns the low 32 bits of the result. The facts also list writes to the copper list pointer register that the decompiled body does not show.

name: disable_interrupts_wait_for_flag
description: Adjusts a 16-bit field and toggles a bit in a shared flag byte, then writes four bytes of a value into memory. It waits in a loop for a flag bit to clear, then writes a mask that clears the interrupt enable bits to disable interrupts, calls two helper routines, and on a status match calls a routine with a fixed memory location. The body ends in bad instruction data and references the text 'highs'.

name: unpack_bitstream_backwards
description: Finds the index of a supplied word in a fixed table, then decodes a bit-packed stream backwards into an output buffer. It reads control bits through the bit-reader helpers, copies literal bytes or repeated runs from earlier output, and finishes by expanding run pairs. It writes a fixed marker byte when a flag equals a fixed value.

name: decode_packed_literals_and_runs
description: The listed facts give only three instructions, but the decompiled body is a bit-driven decoding loop. It reads bits through a helper, writes literal bytes and copies earlier output backwards in runs, then stops when the output pointer reaches the input bound.

name: finish_back_reference_copy
description: Reads bits through a helper and copies a run of earlier output bytes backwards into the output buffer, then continues the decoding loop. It is called by one routine and calls one bit-reader helper.

name: copy_fixed_length_back_reference
description: Copies a run of earlier output bytes backwards into the output buffer, with the run length derived from a bit count read through a helper. It is called by two routines.

name: expand_run_length_pairs
description: Expands pairs of bytes in the packed data, writing each value repeatedly backwards into the output buffer until the input is consumed. It writes a fixed marker byte when a flag equals a fixed value.

name: copy_until_delimiter_byte
description: Copies bytes backwards from the input into the output buffer until it reaches a delimiter byte. It writes a fixed marker byte when a flag equals a fixed value.

name: write_marker_when_flag_set
description: Writes a fixed marker byte three bytes past the base pointer when a flag byte equals a fixed value, then returns.

name: decode_packed_stream_backwards
description: Decodes a bit-packed stream backwards into an output buffer. It reads control bits through the bit-reader helpers and either writes literal bytes or copies runs from earlier output, looping until the output pointer reaches the input bound; the body is 89 instructions long.

name: store_small_and_zero_globals
description: Stores the constant three into one shared global and zero into another, then returns. It is called by four unnamed routines.

name: store_nine_and_large_constant
description: Stores the constant nine into one shared global and the constant one hundred thousand into another, then returns. It is called by four unnamed routines.

name: call_handler_on_block
description: Computes an address from an input register scaled by 512 plus a base pointer, passes it to a routine called through a pointer, and returns zero.

name: dispatch_block_handler_scaled
description: Computes an address from an input register scaled by 512 plus a base pointer, passes it to a routine called through a pointer, and returns zero. It is called by three unnamed routines.

name: wait_for_port_bit_transitions
description: Writes a constant to a record field, then polls a status bit while counting transitions of another bit of the CIA-A port register. It returns after a fixed number of transitions, reading the joystick, mouse or disk status port.

name: spin_forever_idle_loop
description: The body is an infinite loop that does nothing, with the unreachable tail removed, so once entered it never returns. The facts list a video position register access that the decompiled body does not show.

name: jump_to_masked_address
description: Masks an input value to its low 24 bits, calls the routine at that address through a pointer, and returns.

name: boot_entry_single_call
description: The decompiler timed out, so this description rests on the listed facts only. It is the boot block entry reached from the Kickstart strap, makes one call across three instructions, and is called by one routine.

name: relay_boot_block_call
description: The decompiler timed out, so this description rests on the listed facts only. It is referenced by address in the boot block, makes one call across eight instructions, and is called by one routine.

name: xor_decode_and_copy_block
description: Runs two passes over a memory region, XORing each group of four bytes with a running key and copying the decoded bytes to a lower destination. The loop ends at a fixed upper bound, writes a fixed marker constant, and the tail is bad instruction data.

name: forward_helper_result_pair
description: Calls one routine and returns its two-register result unchanged. It is called by six routines and is taken by address.

name: relay_helper_result_pair
description: Calls one routine and returns its two-register result unchanged. It is executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static flow.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Calls one routine and returns. It is called by one routine and runs in the reference trace, and its single call is the whole body.

name: relay_single_routine_call
description: Calls one routine and returns. It is not reached through the static flow, and its single call is the whole body.

name: initialise_four_channel_records
description: Sets a flag bit, calls two routines, then looks up a value from a table indexed by a counter. It initialises four 48-byte channel records with fixed defaults, the table value and a pointer to a shared global, then sets two shared globals to fixed values. The facts list the joystick and disk status port among the registers touched.

name: reset_audio_volume_registers
description: Clears nine shared records and writes fixed constants that the listed facts identify with the four audio volume registers, the audio control register and the DMA control register.

name: set_four_flags_to_one
description: Sets four shared byte flags to one at fixed spacing and returns. The facts list a helper call that the decompiled body does not show.

name: enable_dma_channel_mask
description: When a shared flag is set, it builds a mask with one bit per channel for the four audio channels on top of a fixed base, writes that mask to the DMA control register with the set-enable bit, and sets a second shared value to a fixed value. The facts also list the audio control register.

name: tick_four_channel_sound_sequencer
description: Advances a four-channel sound sequencer once per call when its enable byte is set. For each channel it updates a timer, reads command bytes from a data stream that are dispatched through a jump table, and computes the period and volume values written to the channel records and the audio hardware registers. It sets the DMA enable bits for the channels and calls per-channel routines when the sequencer ends.

name: start_channel_sequence_playback
description: Reads the first command byte from a channel's data pointer, sets up the channel record fields and enters the channel sequencing loop, which updates periods and volumes for the four channels and writes the audio registers. It calls one routine, as the facts show.

name: initialise_channel_and_run_sequence
description: Clears two record bytes, copies two input bytes into the record, sets a flag bit, and enters the channel sequencing loop that updates periods, volumes and DMA enable bits for the four channels.

name: set_channel_start_length_sequence
description: Stores a fixed start pointer and a length of thirty-two into the channel record, then runs the four-channel sequencing loop, which updates each channel's period and volume and writes the audio registers.

name: resume_channel_sequence_loop
description: Stores an input pointer in the channel record, sets the DMA enable mask for the current channel, and runs the four-channel sequencing loop. The facts show it writes the audio DMA and control registers.

name: store_byte_run_sequence
description: The listed facts give two instructions, but the decompiled body stores the first input byte of a channel stream in a shared record field and then runs the four-channel sequencing loop that writes the audio registers.

name: load_channel_header_run_sequence
description: Sets a record byte to a fixed value, copies two header bytes from the input stream into the channel record, clears a flag, and runs the four-channel sequencing loop.

name: clear_flag_run_sequence_loop
description: Clears a record byte, then runs the four-channel sequencing loop starting from the input stream pointer, which updates channel periods and volumes and writes the audio registers.

name: store_slot_byte_run_sequence
description: Stores the first input byte in a channel slot field of the record and then runs the four-channel sequencing loop that updates periods, volumes and DMA enable bits.

name: build_sample_period_table
description: When a flag is clear, walks 38 table entries, storing for each a pointer to its data, a half-length value and a period computed by dividing a fixed constant by the entry's word value. It then sets two data pointers, sets the flag, and reduces six record fields by fixed amounts.

name: select_channel_and_copy_settings
description: Sets two shared flags, selects a channel from an input value and clears its per-channel flag, then copies twelve words into the channel record and computes a per-channel handler pointer from a lookup table. It calls a helper that loads a constant and two other routines, and the facts show it touches the audio control and CIA-A port registers.

name: load_channel_settings_from_input
description: Sets two record fields to fixed values, writes an input word into a shared global, copies twelve words, and sets a channel pointer from a lookup table and a record byte. The facts show it also writes the DMA control register.

name: busy_wait_fixed_count
description: Counts down a fixed count of about 512 iterations to waste time. The facts also list disk pointer, serial data and disk control register accesses that the decompiled body does not show, and the routine is called by three unnamed routines.

name: enable_dma_for_timeout_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so this description rests on the listed facts only. The routine is called by one routine, makes one call across 12 instructions, and writes the DMA control register.

name: record_unexplained_entry_point
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are available. The routine is executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static flow, and its 17 instructions cannot be described further from the evidence.

name: return_without_action
description: The body is only a return, so it does nothing. It is executed in the reference run.

name: return_immediately_entry
description: The body only returns, so it does nothing. It is executed in the reference run.

name: return_immediately_entry
description: The body only returns, so it does nothing. It is taken by address.

name: clear_memory_and_init_hardware
description: Clears nine pairs of words and a large block of memory, stores joystick and status port values in shared globals, and writes constants to the interrupt, DMA, colour and copper control registers. It then restores saved pointers and enables interrupts and DMA from the saved values, and calls seven routines.

name: build_display_copper_table
description: The listed facts show no hardware registers for this entry. When a flag is set it writes a set of constants into a table, then fills a 255-entry table of word pairs that look like copper-list wait and move instructions to colour and display registers; in the flagged branch it loops over eight rows of 32 words, shifting bit fields into each. It calls two routines.

name: call_helper_twice_then_return
description: Calls a helper routine twice in sequence and then returns. The listed facts count 42 instructions and one call, and the decompiled body shows the two calls.

name: combine_nibbles_into_20bit_value
description: Combines the low nibble of the low word, the low word shifted right by four, and the high word shifted left by eight, then masks the result to twenty bits.

name: return_empty_entry_point
description: The decompiled body is only a return, although the listed facts count 37 instructions. The body is taken as a plain return.

name: render_text_glyphs_to_buffer
description: Clears a 127-row buffer when its state is zero, then walks a text string, copying each character's eight-byte glyph into the buffer row by row with a fixed stride, and it handles a newline byte. Otherwise it advances a state counter, and when the counter reaches a fixed value it changes state and calls helpers. The glyph rows are shifted left and right to produce shaded copies.

name: return_without_action_entry
description: The decompiled body is only a return. The listed facts count 28 instructions and one call, which the decompiled body does not show.

name: store_pointer_and_offset_pair
description: Stores the input longword as two words in one pointer pair, and the same longword plus a fixed offset as two words in a second pair. The facts list 123 instructions and two callers, but the decompiled body shows only the stores.

name: start_copper2_wait_raster
description: When a flag bit is set, it writes the second copper list address and the jump register, sets a flag from comparing a byte with a fixed character, and waits until the raster position passes a fixed line. It then calls helpers and clears the flag. The facts also list the keyboard serial register.

name: spin_forever_when_flag_set
description: When a shared flag bit is set, the routine enters an infinite loop, so the write of the flag value that follows is unreachable in the code shown. The facts list the interrupt request and raster position registers, and the routine is taken by address.

name: store_table_sum_deltas
description: Adds two table values selected by offsets held in the record and stores their sum, then fills 255 entries of a word table with the differences between successive sums minus a fixed offset. The stride between entries comes from a record flag, and two record offset bytes are advanced afterwards.

name: xor_bit_pattern_into_bitplane
description: XORs one bit per row across eight bit positions into two screen locations for each of 44 rows, using offsets taken from table values and the record. It then advances four record offset bytes by fixed steps.

name: swap_and_store_screen_pointers
description: Swaps two longword pointers held in the record, computes a second pointer by adding a record offset, and writes the low and high words of these pointers into shared bitplane pointer globals, along with a pointer offset by a fixed amount.

name: configure_cia_timer_interrupt
description: Stores a handler routine address in a shared word, programs the CIA-B timer and control registers with fixed values, and enables interrupt bits through the interrupt enable register. It also clears a counter field in the working record before returning.

name: clear_flag_set_dma_interrupts
description: Clears one bit in a shared flag byte, then writes a fixed sequence of constants to the DMA control and interrupt enable registers. The facts show it also reads the joystick and disk status port, so it is part of the device setup sequence.

name: scale_channel_levels_and_step
description: Calls a setup helper, then multiplies four table bytes by a current level and shifts each product down into spaced words of the working record. It finally moves a level byte one unit toward its previous value.

name: store_scaled_step_difference
description: Multiplies a shared value by a constant and divides the product by the same value, then stores in the working record the byte difference between two successive scaled counter values.

name: run_countdown_sequencer_step
description: Returns zero when a shared enable byte is clear. Otherwise it decrements a countdown in the record, and while it runs it dispatches four channels through a jump table; when it expires it reloads the countdown, clears four table entries, advances a wrapping index and points the record at the next table entry, while also touching the CIA-B timer control register.

name: write_timer_and_request_registers
description: Writes a counter value, a derived value and a copied word to shared globals that the facts identify as the CIA-B interrupt and control registers, the DMA control register and the interrupt request register. The final write sets the top bit of the value, which those registers treat as the enable flag.

name: reset_audio_channel_registers
description: Adjusts a shared value, then writes eight table entries into the pointer and length registers of all four audio channels, followed by a final constant write to the interrupt request register.

name: call_two_helper_routines
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available and the description rests only on the listed facts. The routine is called by one unnamed routine, calls two others across its 59 instructions, and touches no hardware registers.

name: find_table_entry_under_limit
description: Selects a nibble of the input byte according to a phase counter stored in the record, then scans a table row of up to 36 words for the first entry that does not exceed a stored limit. It writes that matching word to an output field, or leaves the output unchanged when the zero flag is set.

name: decrease_position_with_floor
description: Subtracts a delta from a position field in the record and raises the position to a fixed minimum when it falls below that floor. The result is copied into an output field.

name: step_value_toward_target
description: Calls a helper, then moves a position field toward a target field by a step size taken from another field. When the remaining distance is smaller than the step, it snaps the position to the target and copies the result to an output field.

name: add_delta_reset_to_reference
description: Adds a delta to a position field and, when the delta exceeds a second input value, replaces the position with a reference field from the record. The position is then copied to an output field.

name: set_level_offset_when_flagged
description: When the flag byte is nonzero, stores the input nibble byte in the record. It then looks up a table value by an index from the record byte, scales it by the low nibble, negates it when the sign bit is set, and writes the position plus this offset to the output. It adds a shifted amount of the stored byte into a second record field.

name: offset_position_by_table_value
description: Looks up a table value by an index from the record byte, scales it by the low nibble of the stored byte, negates it when the sign bit is set, and writes the position plus this offset to the output. It adds a shifted amount of the stored byte into a second record field.

name: relay_adjust_level_by_nibble
description: Calls a helper, then adjusts a byte level in the record using the input byte. A zero high nibble subtracts the low nibble and clamps the level at zero, while a nonzero high nibble adds it and clamps at a fixed ceiling.

name: adjust_level_by_nibble
description: Adjusts a byte level in the record using the input byte. A zero high nibble subtracts the low nibble and clamps the level at zero, while a nonzero high nibble adds it and clamps at a fixed ceiling.

name: store_level_byte
description: Stores the input byte directly into a level field of the working record and returns.

name: set_index_scaled_clear_counter
description: Stores the input word multiplied by four into an index field of the record and resets a counter field to zero.

name: store_byte_and_call_helper
description: Stores its byte argument into a shared global and then calls a helper routine. The branch for large values assigns the same byte again, so it has no net effect.

name: advance_position_by_stored_step
description: Copies a nonzero input byte into a step field of the record when present. It then adds scaled multiples of that step byte to a 16-bit field and to a 32-bit field, moving both by the stored value.

name: stub_empty_return
description: The routine body is only a return, so it performs no work.
